item.title: Backup and disaster recovery
item.description: Back up the small set of state the controller cannot reconstruct, then rebuild a lost cluster by restoring that state in the right order. Most of what a StageSet manages is recomputed on the next reconcile from your Git repository and your Flux sources, so it needs no backup of its own. Three things are the exception, and losing any of them causes silent data damage rather than a clean failure.

item.title: Inventory and pruning
item.description:
Every time a stage applies, the controller records the exact set of objects it applied, so it can prune what a later revision no longer renders and tear a StageSet down in reverse stage order. That record is the StageInventory — a controller-owned resource you never author (its fields are in the API reference ).

What the inventory records

For each stage, the controller writes a StageInventory listing every object the stage owns — group, kind, namespace, name. On the next reconcile it diffs the new render against that record and prunes the objects that dropped out, honoring prune: false and the conflict policy . On deletion it walks the stages in reverse, so a later stage’s objects are removed before the earlier stages they depend on.
